_doc: Thresholds and rule sets for the draft 7R classification (classify_apps.py). The reviewer confirms or overrides every application in assessment/decisions.json. See references/seven-rs.md. windows_bound_max_files_to_replace: when all Windows-bound findings sit in at most this many files, they are replaced during the port (Replatform) instead of forcing a rehost.

webforms_retain_thresholds._doc: Above either threshold the default for a Web Forms app is retain-on-Framework + hybrid shared libraries; below, UI rewrite.

targets.linux-container: {target} on Linux containers - Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate (or EKS) behind an ALB
targets.linux-worker: {target} Worker Service on Linux - ECS service / scheduled ECS task (EventBridge Scheduler)
targets.linux-batch: {target} console job on Linux - scheduled ECS task (EventBridge Scheduler) or AWS Lambda if short-running
targets.windows-retain: .NET Framework 4.8.1 on Windows - Amazon EC2 Windows (IIS) or ECS Windows containers; shared libraries multi-targeted to netstandard2.0
targets.windows-desktop: .NET 10 Windows Desktop on user machines (optionally Amazon WorkSpaces / AppStream 2.0); back-end calls repointed to AWS
targets.ec2-same-os: Amazon EC2 with the same operating system as today (Windows Server to Windows Server, Linux to Linux); same runtime, IIS / service hosting unchanged

r7_guidance._doc: Per 7R: why not the other Rs (the default reasoning, which the reviewer edits per application), what happens next, the usual risks and who signs off. Rendered with every application plan (classify_apps.py -> report). Sources: AWS Prescriptive Guidance, migration strategies (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/large-migration-guide/migration-strategies.html); Microsoft, ASP.NET to ASP.NET Core migration (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/migration/fx-to-core/).

why_not: Not Retain / Rehost: hosting and patching an application nobody needs costs money and carries security debt.
Not Replatform / Refactor: no business value left to carry forward.
then: Name what replaces the capability: nothing, another application (which screens or calls move there), a SaaS, or a read-only archive.
Find hidden consumers first: IIS logs (last hit per path), service callers (WCF / ASMX / API clients), scheduled jobs, reports reading its database.
Export the data under the retention rule; keep a final backup for the retention period.
Decommission: stop the site, remove DNS and load-balancer entries, revoke service accounts and secrets, remove monitoring and firewall rules, archive the code.
risks: Hidden consumers (partner calls, batch jobs, shared database readers)
A shared database or library that other applications still use

why_not: Not Replatform: a blocker cannot be removed now (unfunded UI rewrite, Windows-only dependency, compliance or a dependency that must move first).
Not Rehost: the client chose to keep it where it is for now (or keep it on Windows in AWS as part of a hybrid).
then: Set a review date and the exit criteria (what must be true to move it).
Keep .NET Framework 4.8.1 and Windows patched.
Move shared libraries to netstandard2.0 (hybrid) so the other applications can move without it.
Record which other applications it blocks (shared database, shared libraries).
risks: Security debt on an ageing stack
It blocks other moves through a shared database or library

why_not: Not Replatform now: Windows-bound dependencies (COM, Office interop, WF, Remoting, MSMQ, unsupported WCF bindings, blocker packages) need replacing first, or a deadline allows no code change.
Not Retain: the data centre exit needs it in AWS.
then: Move the server or IIS site to Amazon EC2 Windows (AWS Application Migration Service or images), same OS.
Secrets from web.config to Secrets Manager / Parameter Store; endpoints and file shares re-pointed.
Plan the follow-up: replace the blocking components, then Replatform.
risks: Keeps Windows and SQL Server licence cost
The follow-up modernisation never gets funded

why_not: Not Rehost: the whole hypervisor estate moves unchanged (for example VMware Cloud on AWS); no per-application work.
then: Infrastructure team moves the VMs; no code change.

why_not: Not Replatform / Refactor: a commodity product (reporting, CMS, fax, HR) covers the needed features for less than porting and running custom code.
then: Map features against the product; plan data export and import.
Rebuild integrations (every caller of this application's services).
Single sign-on, user training, cutover, then Retire the old application.

why_not: Not Rehost: keeps Windows, IIS and the .NET Framework support clock; AWS lists the .NET Framework to .NET port for Linux as a replatform example.
Not Refactor / rewrite: the platform is the only blocker; the domain logic is kept, so the risk is in the port itself, controlled by build, residue and parity gates.
Not Retain: nothing found that cannot move.
then: Port to .NET 10 with one porting engine (AWS DevTx toolkit or AWS Transform); Claude cleans up what it leaves (dotnet-modernization skill).
Shared class libraries first; Linux container on ECS Fargate behind an ALB; managed database.
Record request/response goldens first and replay them against the port.
risks: Behaviour drift: path case, culture, time zones, line endings, serialisation defaults

why_not: Not Replatform: part of the application has no .NET 10 counterpart (Web Forms UI, WCF bindings not in CoreWCF, MSMQ) or cannot meet demand as built, so that part is rewritten.
Not Retain: the rewrite is small enough, or the client funds it.
then: Rewrite only the slice that has no counterpart (UI, a service boundary); port the rest as in Replatform.
Incrementally: YARP in front of the old application, routes moved one at a time, System.Web adapters for shared libraries and session, then remove the old route.
Characterisation tests and parity before each route moves.
risks: Business-rule drift in the rewritten slice

webforms_token_ui._doc: A Web Forms project whose UI is a token (a few pages and markup under this share of its hand-written lines) is a service with a page or two, not a UI application: Replatform, with the pages rewritten inside the port.
